Biden was indeed replaced as the Democratic nominee following his poor debate performance, but by Kamala Harris, not Gavin Newsom, and the general election was Trump vs. Harris, not Trump vs. Newsom.

While Trump did win the November 2024 election, it was a relatively narrow victory in the popular vote (about 1.5 points) and a modest Electoral College margin, not the described landslide, and this was after Biden had already been swapped for Harris, altering the conditional's premise.

Trump did later develop a much friendlier posture toward EVs/Tesla following his alliance with Elon Musk starting mid-2024, but a clean, sudden public pro-EV policy reversal within 30 days of June 7, 2024 did not occur; the warming took shape more gradually over the following months.

The premise of this conditional prediction (Biden not being swapped out) did not hold, since Biden withdrew from the race in late July 2024, so the prediction's specific scenario was never tested as stated.

The Texas Stock Exchange did file its Form 1 SEC registration in January 2025 (roughly matching the 'later this year/next year' framing, shifted by about six months) and received SEC approval in September 2025, with its first listings anticipated for late 2026, broadly tracking the predicted timeline though slightly delayed relative to the original 2024/2025/2026 filing-trading-listing sequence.

The 2024 Atlantic hurricane season was indeed unusually active and destructive, featuring two Category 5 storms (Beryl and Milton) and becoming the third-costliest season on record, consistent with forecasts of larger, stronger, more frequent hurricanes.
